rule_level_problems.problem: The pre-screen that triggers the 'Check for anaphylaxis' task omits the page's group 4 (abdominal pain / vomiting) and the exposure findings from its any2 list. A patient presenting with, e.g., a recent medication and difficulty breathing plus vomiting meets Q3 ('>= 2 of') on the page, but here only Difficulty breathing counts, the possible diagnosis does not fire, and the exposure/allergy questions are never asked. Identical to the gold standard's pre-screen, so this is an inherited gap rather than a builder error.

'Sudden onset' is applied only to the four skin findings in the Q3 any2 and the Q4 skin group; difficulty breathing, BP, dizziness, collapse, abdominal pain and vomiting are unqualified, although the page's 'sudden onset of >= 2 of' governs every group. 'In the few hours before symptoms started' is not expressed on any exposure finding. Both choices mirror the gold.

Q1's 'has caused anaphylaxis before' is approximated by (allergy X), which also matches a mild known allergy; SNOMED has per-substance 'Anaphylaxis caused by fish / egg / tree nut / venom' disorders that would be closer, but the gold uses the same proxy. 'Food' is limited to the five footnote foods although the footnote is illustrative.

rule_level_problems.problem: Evidence is the onset form (> (onset <finding>) (time_ago 4 weeks)) while the check_for holds the bare findings. The briefing says onset works in due_to positions, but the 'probable evidence must be checked for' test matches by exact s-expression string; if the test does not unwrap onset, all four rhinitis criteria will be flagged as not checked for. Worth confirming with the per-page checker.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable eczema in previous anaphylaxis
rule_level_problems.problem: Requires three separately recorded findings (sited Scaly skin, Xeroderma, Itching of skin) for what the page describes as one observation; strict conjunction may under-fire, and Itching of skin is also a required part of the urticaria rule, so an itchy patient with both scaly patches and a wheal gets both diagnoses. Acceptable reading of the page, flagged for awareness.

Priority is tied to (active_condition Anaphylaxis), so it only fires once a clinician accepts the probable diagnosis; the page's header addresses the patient with 'possible' anaphylaxis. Same pattern as the gold; no page-justified level mismatch.

summary: The red-box flowchart is encoded faithfully and matches the gold standard structure (Q1 exposure+allergy pairs, Q2 exposure with any2 of four groups, Q4 skin sign plus any-of), with only inherited approximations: no 'few hours' window, Sudden onset applied only to the skin group, allergy standing in for prior anaphylaxis, and a possible-anaphylaxis pre-screen that omits abdominal pain/vomiting so some Q3-positive presentations never trigger the check. The 'other allergy' table is fully covered with correct rule types (asthma possible, the four 'likely' probable), gated on History of anaphylaxis, which nothing on the page records; the remaining gaps are unrepresentable qualifiers ('most days', 'disappear within 24 hours', bilateral watering). All SNOMED concepts used exist and mean what the page says.
